description: Show photos whenever someone asks about or mentions a famous person, place, film, show, game, animal, car or product.

offer.reason: owner ruling 2026-10-10: on for adults below the 85% recall bar; re-run later, back off if worse

author: MaiPai

examples: what does the Eiffel Tower look like
what does a koala look like
show me the Golden Gate Bridge
the Pontiac Fiero was a great-looking car

subject.description: The thing to show, by its full proper name as in the conversation, for example "Pontiac Fiero", "Stranger Things", "Eiffel Tower". A follow-up like "what does he look like" means the previous message's subject. Use this when they ask what something looks like, ask who or what a well-known thing is, or are chatting about a thing whose look matters (artwork too), for example "that old Ford Mustang was a beautiful car" means subject "Ford Mustang", "I just watched Jaws again" means subject "Jaws" and "what is the PlayStation 5" means subject "PlayStation 5"; never for advice, how-to, maths, code, news facts, feelings or anything with nothing to look at. Call it in short, casual replies too. The app shows the photos itself; never mention them.

kind.description: What kind of thing it is, in one to three words, from the conversation: for example "animal", "TV series", "car", "planet", "snake", "programming language".

data_sources.destination: Wikidata, Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons (wikidata.org, en.wikipedia.org, commons.wikimedia.org)
data_sources.when: a written answer is about a well-known thing you can look at and pictures are on for you
data_sources.what: the name of the thing, nothing about you or your question
data_sources.retention: controlled entirely by the Wikimedia Foundation; see their own privacy policy

data_sources.destination: the sites that host the pictures, through Home itself
data_sources.when: the same answers, to fetch a few pictures and check they are real
data_sources.what: an ordinary picture request from Home, with no cookie and no referrer

data_sources.destination: your own SearXNG instance, for things that are not people
data_sources.when: the same answers, when web search is set up
data_sources.what: the name of the thing, at your own safe-search level
data_sources.retention: whatever your own SearXNG instance keeps
